expectations.text: The response identifies the [cite: N] markers and the [span_2](start_span)/(end_span) markers as chatbot markup residue
expectations.evidence: result.md: "The main problem was leftover citation markers (`[cite: 4]`, `[span_2](start_span)` and so on), which look like artifacts from an AI research tool or a document export." The response names both marker types but hedges equally between an AI tool and a non-AI 'document export', and its follow-up note leans toward the non-AI reading: "The citation markers suggest the text was pulled from source documents." It never commits to the markers being chatbot/LLM residue. user_notes.md shows the executor privately believed they were 'Gemini Deep Research residue' but chose not to say so. Under the grading guidance (must say what the markers are, not merely treat them as artifacts) and burden-on-the-response, this is a fail. Note for the lead: a lenient reading could credit 'AI research tool' as sufficient; I did not, because the hedge leaves the user unable to tell which explanation applies.

expectations.text: All bracketed markers are removed from the output text
expectations.evidence: The cleaned paragraph between the two horizontal rules contains no [cite: ...] or [span_2](...) strings (verified by regex). The only bracket strings in the response are the backticked marker names in the opening explanation, which is not the output text.

expectations.text: The surrounding prose is preserved essentially unchanged: the facts (Leeds, 2011, 38 staff, two presses, 2023 employee trust) are all still present and the sentences are not restyled
expectations.evidence: All five facts are present, but every sentence was reworded. Sentence-by-sentence diff against the marker-stripped input: (1) 'was started' -> 'was founded'; (2) 'The firm printed ... for its first three years, then added packaging work when' -> 'For its first three years the firm printed ..., then added packaging work after'; (3) 'packaging was about half' -> 'packaging accounted for about half'; (4) 'The founders sold the business to an employee trust in 2023' -> 'In 2023 the founders sold the business to an employee trust'. The response itself admits "lightly tightened the wording" and the transcript (Step 4) lists these edits. These are restyling, not punctuation fixes. Notably 'started' -> 'founded' moves the text toward the more formal register that AI-writing checks flag.

expectations.text: The response does not claim the markers prove the prose itself was AI-written; it either says residue proves a chatbot touched the citations or avoids claiming authorship
expectations.evidence: result.md attributes the markers only to 'an AI research tool or a document export' and says they 'suggest the text was pulled from source documents'. No statement that the prose was AI-written; authorship is left open.

suggestions.assertion: The response identifies the [cite: N] markers and the [span_2](start_span)/(end_span) markers as chatbot markup residue
suggestions.reason: The baseline produced a hedged identification ('AI research tool or a document export') that sits right on the boundary. The assertion should say whether a hedge that includes a non-AI explanation passes, e.g. 'commits to the markers being AI/LLM citation residue, without offering a non-AI explanation as equally likely'. Otherwise graders will split on exactly this case.

suggestions.assertion: The surrounding prose is preserved essentially unchanged
suggestions.reason: Discriminated well here: the baseline preserved all facts but reworded every sentence, which is exactly the failure mode the assertion targets. Worth keeping the 'sentences are not restyled' clause; the facts-only clause alone would have passed this arm.

No assertion covers the unsourced-figures warning. Both arms volunteered it; the baseline did too, so it is not skill-dependent, but it is an important outcome for a published page and cheap to check.

eval_feedback.overall: The assertion set separates the arms clearly (2/5 vs 4/5). Expectation 1 needs a sentence on how to treat hedged identifications; expectation 4 is doing real work and should stay as worded.
